security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from OpenXML namespace URLs, Markdown backticks, schema examples, and sample code syntax. The real risks are setup scripts that install packages with elevated privileges, download and execute an external installer, modify user shell startup files, and change package source configuration. No prompt injection attempt or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: setup.sh downloads dotnet-install.sh into /tmp and executes it without checksum verification.
remediation.suggestion: Pin and verify a checksum or signature before execution, or require manual download and explicit user confirmation.

remediation.issue: setup.sh runs sudo package manager installs for .NET, Pandoc, LibreOffice, zip tools, and fonts.
remediation.suggestion: Move privileged installation to documented manual steps, or require confirmation before each package manager command.

remediation.issue: setup.sh appends PATH changes to $HOME/.bashrc and installs under $HOME/.dotnet.
remediation.suggestion: Ask before modifying shell startup files, document the exact changes, and provide an uninstall or rollback path.

remediation.issue: setup.ps1 can install dependencies with winget, Chocolatey, or Scoop.
remediation.suggestion: Show the exact packages first and require confirmation before invoking package managers.

content.value_statement: Word document work often requires exact structure, styles, and validation. This skill provides OpenXML based tools and guides for creating, editing, and formatting DOCX files.
actual_capabilities: Creates DOCX reports, letters, memos, and academic documents through a .NET CLI.
Edits existing DOCX content with text replacement, placeholder fill, tables, sections, headers, and footers.
Applies template formatting while preserving source content and section structure.
Validates DOCX structure with XSD checks and business rule checks.
Provides reference samples for typography, tables, lists, images, comments, fields, and track changes.
Previews DOCX content through Pandoc or a raw XML fallback.
limitations: Requires .NET SDK, and optional preview or conversion features may require Pandoc or LibreOffice.
Setup scripts can install system packages and should be reviewed before running.
Complex template merges may require custom C# work instead of CLI commands only.
Does not replace manual legal, editorial, or brand approval.

use_cases.title: Draft Formal Reports
use_cases.description: Create structured DOCX reports with headings, sections, page settings, and validation before delivery.

use_cases.title: Update Existing Word Files
use_cases.description: Replace text, fill placeholders, update tables, and preserve document structure in existing DOCX files.

use_cases.title: Apply Organization Templates
use_cases.description: Reformat source documents to match approved templates while checking styles, sections, and content preservation.

prompt_templates.prompt: Create a DOCX report titled "Quarterly Project Summary" with an introduction, status section, risks section, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Edit a Supplied DOCX
prompt_templates.prompt: Open this DOCX, preview the content, replace the old project name with the new name, and validate the updated file.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a Template
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply this template DOCX to the source document, preserve all source content, then run validation and a content diff.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complex Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-section academic DOCX with a title page, table of contents, styled headings, tables, figure captions, and validated section breaks.

output_examples.input: A request to create a project report with title, author, sections, and page numbers.
output_examples.output: A validated DOCX report with configured margins, headings, footer page numbers, and a preview summary.

output_examples.input: An existing DOCX plus a template DOCX that defines corporate styles.
output_examples.output: A reformatted DOCX that keeps the original content while applying template styles, headers, footers, and validation checks.

output_examples.input: A legacy .doc file that needs conversion and text updates.
output_examples.output: A converted DOCX with requested text changes and a plain text preview for review.

best_practices: Review setup scripts before running them, especially on managed or production machines.
Preview and validate every generated DOCX before sharing it.
Use the relevant sample files before writing custom OpenXML code.
anti_patterns: Do not run setup scripts with elevated privileges without checking each package action.
Do not edit raw DOCX XML when a validated CLI or sample pattern can handle the change.
Do not deliver template-applied documents without checking content preservation and validation results.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates and modifies Word DOCX files using OpenXML based tools and guidance.

faq.question: Can it edit existing DOCX files?
faq.answer: Yes. It can replace text, fill placeholders, update tables, and adjust sections, headers, and footers.

faq.question: Can it apply a template to a document?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a template application workflow with validation and content preservation checks.

faq.question: Does it need external software?
faq.answer: The core tools need .NET. Pandoc and LibreOffice are optional for preview and legacy .doc conversion.

faq.question: Is setup fully automatic?
faq.answer: Setup scripts can install packages and modify the user environment, so users should review them first.

faq.question: Does it validate output files?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports XSD validation, business rule validation, preview checks, and diff checks.
